wu: Students play 'Find Someone Who' with future intentions prompts like 'Find someone who is going to travel next month'. They mingle, ask 'Are you going to...?', and write names. They report back: 'Ali is going to travel because he wants to see his family.'
wuAlt: Students draw a simple future plan on a sticky note and guess classmates' plans: 'Is she going to study?' 'Yes, she is because she wants to pass the exam.'
Students play 'Memory Race' with picture cards showing future actions (e.g., plane, book, diploma). They flip cards and make sentences: 'He is going to fly because he has a job.'
pres: Show flashcards of a man packing a bag and a woman buying a book. Model: 'He is going to travel because he has a holiday. She is going to study because she has an exam.' Check understanding by asking 'Why is he going to travel?' and eliciting 'because he has a holiday.'
presAlt: Use a simple story about a boy who wants to be a doctor. Draw a picture of him with a stethoscope: 'He is going to study medicine because he wants to help people.'
Bring realia: a map, a textbook, a calendar. Point and say: 'I am going to use the map because I want to go to Casablanca. I am going to read the book because I want to learn English.'
prac: Students do 'Going to Dominoes' matching cards with pictures and reasons (e.g., picture of cooking + 'because I want to eat'). In pairs, they place cards and say the full sentence. Monitor and correct errors like 'He go to' instead of 'He is going to'.
pracAlt: Play 'Sentence Auction' with correct/incorrect sentences about future plans. Students bid on true sentences like 'She is going to swim because it's hot.'
Do 'Chain Drill': Student A says 'I am going to cook tonight.' Student B repeats and adds 'because I am hungry.' Student C repeats and adds, 'so I am going to buy food.'
ls: Students listen to a short audio of three people talking about their weekend plans. They tick the correct reason from a list (e.g., 'Why is Fatima going to the market? a) She needs food b) She wants to meet friends'). Check answers by replaying and pausing at 'because'.
re: After break, play 'Simon Says' with future actions: 'Simon says: Pretend you are going to travel.' Students mime and say 'I am going to travel because I have a ticket.'
prod: In groups of 3, students plan a one-day trip to Oujda using a worksheet with prompts: 'Where are you going? What are you going to do? Why?' They present their plan: 'We are going to the old medina because we want to buy spices. We are going to eat tagine because we are hungry.'
rw: Students read a short paragraph about 'Amina's Plans' and underline all 'because' and 'so' sentences. Then, they write 3 simple sentences about their own plans using 'going to' and 'because', e.g., 'I am going to call my mother because I miss her.'
st: Sing a simple chant: 'What are you going to do? I'm going to learn, because it's new! What are you going to see? I'm going to travel, because I want to be free!' Close with: 'Today we learned to explain plans with going to and because. Thank you, class.'
g: Students write 6 future plans on a grid (e.g., 'go to the cinema'). Teacher reads sentences like 'He is going to watch a movie', and students cross off matching plans.
Teams race to match picture cards (e.g., umbrella) with reason cards (e.g., 'because it might rain') and make a full sentence.
One student draws a future plan (e.g., a plane), others guess 'Are you going to travel?' and ask 'Why?'
Students act out future actions (e.g., studying) while others say 'He is going to study because he has a test.'
Groups unscramble word cards to make correct 'going to' sentences with 'because', e.g., 'She / going to / buy / because / she needs / food / is'.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a short paragraph about their ideal future using 3 'going to' sentences with 'because' and 'so'.
Support / weaker learners: Use sentence frames: 'I am going to ______ because ______.' with picture prompts.
hw: Option 1: Interview a family member about their weekend plans and write 2 sentences using 'going to' and 'because'.
Option 2: Draw 3 pictures of your future plans and label them with 'going to' and 'because' sentences.
Option 3: Complete a worksheet with 5 gaps to fill in 'going to' or 'because' in sentences about plans.
tip: For adults, connect language to real-life goals like work or family. Use Moroccan examples (e.g., 'I am going to learn English because I want a better job') to increase relevance and motivation.
